ov: A heavy-set, fox-like wild dog of East Asia, named for its raccoon-like face. Unusually for a dog, it hibernates through cold winters and can climb trees. It was brought to Europe for the fur trade and has spread so widely that the EU now lists it as invasive.

why.h: The only member of the dog family known to hibernate, putting on fat in early winter to get through it.

wt: About 3 kg in March; males 6.5–7 kg by late summer
rg: Native to East Asia; the closely related tanuki lives in Japan. Introduced and invasive across much of Europe.
df: Almost anything: insects, rodents, frogs and toads, birds, fish, reptiles, molluscs and crabs.
fx: In Japanese folklore the tanuki is a mischievous, jolly master of disguise and shapeshifting.
Since 2019 it has been illegal to import, sell or release it anywhere in the European Union.
